title: Fleet oscillation damper and reserve smoothing + utilization trend telemetry
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce an oscillation damper for autoscaler decisions, add reserve-smoothing operator to prevent rapid capacity flips, and publish utilization-trend metrics for SLO alerting and capacity planning.
description:
Context and motivation: Rapid minute-to-minute demand spikes were causing autoscaler flip-flopping in mixed-tenant pools. Recent incidents showed healthy tenants losing short-lived capacity because the scaler reacted to transient utilization bursts then reversed decisions when the signal decayed. This PR introduces a light-weight 'oscillation damper' for the fleet autoscaler, a reserve-smoothing operator that preserves short-term reserve capacity when scaling down, and a parallel utilization-trend telemetry pipeline so SREs and product teams can reason about drift and preemptive scaling needs.

What this changes (high level):
- Autoscaler: add oscillation_damper stage (EWMA+hold-down window) that attenuates sensitivity to high-frequency utilization noise and enforces a minimum hold time for downscales.
- Reserve smoother: maintain a small, configurable reserve budget (per-pool) that decays slowly to avoid immediate decommits after spikes. The smoother is configurable with nogo thresholds and percent-based buffers.
- Per-tenant burst leash: a soft cap that prevents transient tenants from consuming >X% of warm capacity for more than Y seconds; leases are recorded and exposed via telemetry.
- Telemetry: add utilization_trend_{minute,5m,30m} series (counter+gauge mix) and a trend_score gauge that feeds into anomaly detection + capacity planning dashboards. Metrics are exported to Prometheus and surfaced in Console.
- E2E tests and loadbench scenarios: new deterministic tests that assert absence of oscillation under synthetic burst patterns.

Implementation notes:
- Oscillation damper computes a short EWMA (alpha=0.2 default) over the per-pool 95th-percentile token utilization and keeps a downscale hold window (default 120s) during which scale-downs are suppressed unless utilization falls below the smoothed reserve threshold.
- Reserve smoother keeps a soft-reserve ledger per-pool and decays it with a 1/t decay constant to slowly return capacity to the pool. This was implemented as a separate controller module so it can be toggled via feature flag.
- Burst leash is applied at admission-time in the headroom allocator and emits lease events when invoked; collectors aggregate lease counts per-tenant for 1h windows.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit tests: damper and smoother modules covered with deterministic time mocks.
- Integration: ran scaled loadbench against a 50-node cluster (local perf lab) with synthetic tenants; observed 72% reduction in scale flapping events and 18% lower wasted provisioning time across the test window.
- CI: all checks passed (build, unit, integration smoke). Canary rollout to a single low-traffic pool for 24h before global rollout.

CI checks summary: build: pass; unit: pass; integration-smoke: pass; lint: pass; loadbench: pass. CI run id: ci/2026/02/24/8423.

Configuration and rollout plan:
- Feature flag: autoscaler.oscillation_damper.enabled = false by default. We will enable the feature flag in 1 pool (canary) for 24h, then a 10% traffic rollout followed by full rollout if no regressions. Reserve smoother and burst leash are toggled independently.
- Default conservative knobs chosen for GA: EWMA alpha=0.2, downscale_hold=120s, reserve_buffer=5% of pool capacity, burst_leash_limit=30% warm capacity over 20s.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- No DB migrations. Reserve smoother persists ephemeral ledger in existing fleet state store and will tolerate missing entries.
- Config schema changes are additive; default values preserve existing autoscaler behavior when feature flags off.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misconfigured hold window could delay necessary downscales, increasing cost. Mitigation: conservative defaults + rollout gating + per-pool cost alerts.
- Risk: telemetry cardinality growth. Mitigation: metrics are emitted at pool/tenant-aggregated windows only; added sample caps in exporter.

Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-28. Merge commit: a3f7b2e4c1d9e6b2a4b8f9c5e6d7f80211223344.

Related work and follow-ups:
- ENG-3245: per-tenant hold-down policy (planned).
- ENG-3301: refine lease accounting for cross-pool spillovers.
- Docs: ops/autoscaler-tuning.md updated with new knobs and recommended values.

Notes for on-call: enable the trend dashboard and watch suppressed_downscale_count and reserve_utilization_ratio during rollout. If suppressed_downscale_count spikes beyond expected thresholds and capacity usage remains high, consider temporarily reducing downscale_hold or disabling oscillator for affected pool.
